Develop and maintain operational and production-support scripts. Create ad hoc queries for data analysis, reporting, reconciliation, validation, and issue resolution. APIs and service-based integrations. File-based data transfers and batch interfaces. Upstream and downstream application dependencies. Data validation, reconciliation, exception handling, and feed monitoring. Experience supporting high-volume data processing, batch jobs, ETL workflows, data conversion, data migration, and data-reconciliation processes. Working knowledge of database application design, data modeling, schema development, and database object management sufficient to maintain and enhance scalable, reliable database solutions. Experience deploying SQL, PL/SQL, schema, and configuration changes through structured development, testing, validation, and production-release processes. Familiarity with source control, code review, release documentation, rollback planning, and automated or repeatable database deployment practices. Complementary Oracle database administration experience, including working knowledge of: Oracle RAC. RMAN backup and recovery. Oracle Data Guard. Database security, roles, privileges, and auditing. Tablespaces, storage, sessions, locks, and database-object management. Production monitoring, incident troubleshooting, and recovery procedures. Develop ad hoc queries and scripts to support investigations, reporting, reconciliation, data correction, and operational requests. Maintain and enhance PL/SQL packages, procedures, functions, triggers, batch jobs, and database interfaces. Monitor, troubleshoot, and maintain data feeds involving Oracle, Apache NiFi, AWS endpoints, APIs, files, and connected applications. Investigate failed or incomplete data flows and coordinate resolution across database, integration, application, and infrastructure teams. Perform data validation and root-cause analysis to identify discrepancies between source and target systems. Support application releases, database deployments, production incidents, and post-deployment validation. Tune SQL and PL/SQL workloads to improve performance, scalability, and reliability. Partner with Oracle DBAs on database configuration, RAC, recovery, Data Guard, security, performance, and environment-related issues. Ability to work effectively with developers, database administrators, application owners, business analysts, infrastructure teams, and upstream and downstream integration partners. review_candidates.title: UNFPA Egypt CO - National Consultancy for the preparation to conduct the 2028 Population and Housing Census
review_candidates.description: Job Description Hiring Office: Egypt Country Office/UNFPA Purpose of consultancy: The Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) of Egypt is preparing to conduct the 2028 Population and Housing Census using a Combined Census Methodology (Base Register + Full Field Enumeration). This approach aligns with UN Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses (Revision 4). This approach combines administrative register data with field enumeration and can leverage both registers and field operations as it provides the opportunity to assess the accuracy and completeness of the available administrative data sources. In this design, administrative registers provide the population baseline and select core topics, while full field enumeration verifies data on the doorstep and collects characteristics unavailable in registers. Also, it will serve as a foundational milestone toward a fully register-based census model in future rounds. The overall purpose of this assignment is to strengthen CAPMAS’s institutional and technical capacity to assess, clean, link, and utilize administrative registers for the 2028 Combined Census and the subsequent transition to register-based statistics. This technical assistance aims to establish the statistical infrastructure within CAPMAS required to transform raw administrative files into high-quality statistical records, build an integrated secondary Statistical Population Register (SPR), and implement microdata confidentiality safeguards. Scope of work: (Description of services, activities, or outputs) Transitioning to a register-based census is especially challenging for populous countries like Egypt due to the volume of data that must be integrated. Additionally, some administrative registers are often decentralized across regional and local levels rather than centralized nationally, significantly increasing the number of data sources to process and further complicating the transition. As part of census modernization, and as a strategic secondary consideration, integration of Mobile Phone Data for Population Statistics is another important consideration. Mobile phone data—specifically anonymized and aggregated Call Detail Records (CDRs) and positioning data—offers a high-coverage source for producing frequent, timely, and dynamic population statistics. Within the scope of this consultancy, mobile phone data will be evaluated at a conceptual and methodology-design level as a supplementary "signs of life" tool to validate register population counts, while primary execution remains focused on administrative registers. While CAPMAS holds deep and long-standing expertise in traditional census operations and information management, a register-based statistical system requires additional statistical expertise, particularly in the linkage and matching of data in registers, record linkage, quality assessment and statistical control. To ensure international compliance and rigorous standards, this technical assistance is grounded in the United Nations Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses (Revision 4), the UNSD Handbook on Register-Based Population and Housing Censuses, and the UNECE Guidelines for Assessing the Quality of Administrative Sources for Use in Censuses. The administrative records in Egypt are primarily managed by various ministries and register-holders, CAPMAS will build an internal, secondary Statistical Population Register (SPR). This consultancy will enable CAPMAS technical teams to assess register readiness, execute administrative-to-statistical data transformations, build an integrated SPR backbone, and implement statistical data protection. Objectives of the Assignment Preconditions Assessment: Evaluate and benchmark Egypt’s register ecosystem against international preconditions for register-based and hybrid transitions, highlighting legal, technical, and institutional gaps. Multi-Stage Data Quality Assessment: Train and enable CAPMAS to identify and evaluate administrative data sources across Source, Input, Process, and Output quality stages. Data Transformation and Matching: Establish specialized capacity in deterministic and probabilistic record linkage, de-duplication, conflict resolution, and "Signs of Life" (SOL) activity filtering. SPR Structural Construction: Formulate the architectural blueprint and operational workflow to link individuals, addresses, and enterprises into an integrated secondary Statistical Population Register. Data Governance & Safeguards: Establish statistical disclosure control, microdata security, and inter-institutional governance frameworks. Comprehensive Scope of Work & Technical Modules Module 1: Readiness and Preconditions for Register Transitions This module establishes the foundational non-technical and institutional parameters required to secure a reliable, continuous, and lawful supply of administrative data. Legal Framework & Political Support: Review CAPMAS's legal authority under Law No. 35 of 1960 and relevant modern statistics acts to receive, process, merge, and store microdata from administrative owners strictly for statistical purposes, ensuring confidentiality. Also, a strong political commitment and formalized collaboration between administrative authorities and the national statistical office are essential for a successful transition to register-based statistics. Administrative Routines Assessment: Assess the current data collection routines, capacities and quality guidelines of partner agencies to ensure a continuous and dependable supply of high-quality data. Unified Identifier Evaluation: Assess the penetration, stability, and error rates of the 14-digit National ID across external registers. Inter-Institutional Frameworks: Draft templates for Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), data sharing protocols, Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs), and Service Level Agreements (SLAs) between the holders of administrative registers (Administrative Control, MoHP, MoSS, etc) and CAPMAS defining transmission frequencies, format standards, metadata sharing, and dispute resolution. Public Trust and Data Ethics: Establish transparency frameworks, data ethics assessments, and public communications regarding data anonymization and confidentiality. Other relevant points to be considered: Data provision: Where appropriate, and with necessary safeguards in place, explore opportunities for collaboration with the private sector to access data that can support census operations. This might involve accessing through data-sharing agreements, private sector data such as mobile location data or utility usage records, which can be valuable for understanding population mobility or identifying signs of life. Resolving Data Overlaps and Conflicts: A combined census often draws on multiple data sources that may contain overlapping or conflicting variables. In such cases, decision-makers must evaluate and select the most appropriate source to use. Furthermore, register-based data and field data frequently yield inconsistent results, even for identical topics. To ensure coherence, weighting techniques can be applied to align the datasets, while field data can serve as a benchmark to evaluate the accuracy and coverage of register counts. Module 2: The Four-Stage Register Quality Evaluation Framework Capacity building must follow the UNECE/UNSD four-stage quality evaluation framework to systematically assess quality across the entire data journey. CAPMAS and the Expert will consider splitting the training into two phases, one on assessing the registers and two on developing the statistical population register: Source-Level Quality: Evaluating legal basis, register keeper trust, metadata completeness, and data transfer logistics. Input-Level Quality: Assessing raw microdata completeness, representation errors (under-coverage and over-coverage), measurement errors, and timestamp alignment. Process-Level Quality: Measuring linkage accuracy (false positives vs. false negatives), imputation rates, and edit failure rates. Output-Level Quality: Validating accuracy, relevance, coherence, and comparability with past census benchmarks. Module 3: Administrative-to-Statistical Transformation & Linkage This module covers the core statistical algorithms and processing rules required to integrate disparate databases into a single coherent census database. Concept and Classification Harmonization: Mapping administrative concepts (e.g., registered address, formal employment) to UN census definitions (e.g., usual residence, labor force status). Deterministic and Probabilistic Record Linkage: Training on matching algorithms using common identifiers (PINs) as well as non-unique identifiers (name, sex, date of birth, geographic codes). De-duplication and Conflict Resolution Rules: Establishing decision-tree logic and priority rules (weighting recency, source reliability, and cross-register agreement) when handling contradictory entries across sources. Signs of Life (SOL) Methodology: Implementing SOL activity markers (e.g., active health visits, school enrolment, tax/pension contributions, utility activity) to filter out latent over-coverage (unreported emigrations/deaths) from the baseline population. Module 4: Establishing the Statistical Population Register (SPR) and Base Registers CAPMAS will be guided in designing the conceptual and database architecture of an internal, secondary Statistical Population Register that serves as the backbone for census operations. Architectural Blueprint: Designing the SPR architecture within CAPMAS, linking individual statistical IDs to base registers: oStatistical Population Register (SPR): Serving as the national population spine. oBuilding/Dwelling Register & Master Address File: Linking individual usual residence to physical coordinates (𝑥,𝑦) and structural units. oStatistical Business Register (SBR): Linking working individuals to enterprise locations for workplace/industry statistics. Pre-filling Field Enumeration: Formulate pre-filling rules for the 2028 combined census field instruments. Train CAPMAS on how register-based data can be securely pre-filled onto tablets for doorstep verification and updating by field enumerators, managing the risk of enumerator bias. Triangulation and Benchmarking: Develop methods to triangulate administrative register counts, mobile phone estimates, and full field enumeration results to evaluate coverage and adjust statistical weights. Module 5: Microdata Protection, Anonymization & Confidentiality This module operates strict data protection protocols to prevent the disclosure of individual and institutional identities. Data Masking and Hashing: Implementing secure, automated one-way hashing algorithms to replace administrative National IDs with pseudonymous internal Statistical IDs. Statistical Disclosure Control (SDC): Applying SDC tools for small-area tabulations to preserve individual confidentiality. Five Safes Framework: Designing operational protocols around Safe Data, Safe Projects, Safe People, Safe Settings, and Safe Outputs. Duration and working schedule: The consultancy will span a period of 12 weeks, structured into four sequential integrated phases: Phase 1: Inception and Baseline Gap Analysis: Audit current CAPMAS administrative data holdings, existing MoUs with line ministries, and current legal/technical readiness. Benchmark CAPMAS against UN/UNFPA preconditions and submit a gap analysis report. (Approx 10 days) Phase 2: Tailored Curriculum and Sandbox Development: Design training modules and build a synthetic/anonymized "sandbox" database reflecting typical Egyptian administrative data structures (e.g., civil status, education, supply cards) for hands-on technical labs. Phase 3: Capacity Building Workshop Delivery: Deliver a 12-day practical training program for 20–30 CAPMAS statisticians, database engineers, and census planners covering record linkage, SOL logic, and quality evaluation matrices. (Approx 12 days) Phase 4: Pilot SPR Construction and Operational Guidelines: Guide CAPMAS teams in constructing a prototype Statistical Population Register (SPR) using real test datasets. Co-draft Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for data quality assessment, transformation algorithms, and SDC for the 2028 census. (Approx 10 days) Place where services are to be delivered: Basically, within CAPMAS premises with visits to relevant key stakeholders as required and coordinated by CAPMAS Delivery dates and how work will be delivered (e.g. electronic, hard copy etc.): Inception & Readiness Report Comprehensive baseline gap analysis evaluating CAPMAS against UN/UNFPA register transition preconditions, legal mandates, PIN availability and inter-institutional agreements. End of Week 3 Training Package Complete curriculum, technical lecture slides, R/Python/SQL scripts for record linkage/SOL, and a synthetic test dataset. End of Week 5 Training Delivery Delivery of 12-day hands-on technical training for 20-30 designated CAPMAS technical personnel. End of Week 8 Prototype SPR Architecture & Codebase Documented database schema and automated codebase for linking registers, applying multi-source conflict resolution rules, and executing 'Signs of Life' filtration. End of Week 11 Final Report & Operational SOPs Final report summarizing outcomes, recommended MoU templates, Data Quality Assessment Matrices, and SDC Guidelines for the 2028 Hybrid Census. End of Week 12 Deliverables 1, 2, & 4: Submitted electronically in bilingual format (English and Arabic). Deliverable 3: Training completion report containing attendance logs, participant evaluation forms, and pre- and post-workshop assessment scores. Microsoft 365 er ein sentral plattform for kommunikasjon, samhandling og informasjonsdeling i kommunen. Vi ønskjer å forvalte plattforma meir heilskapleg, utnytte funksjonaliteten betre og gje tilsette og leiarar god støtte i bruken av verktøya. Samtidig skal kommunen ta i bruk kunstig intelligens på ein kontrollert og ansvarleg måte, mellom anna gjennom Microsoft Copilot og andre aktuelle KI-verktøy. Stillinga passar for deg som har god forståing for Microsoft 365, likar å arbeide praktisk med teknologi og gjere funksjonalitet og moglegheiter forståeleg for andre. Du må kunne veksle mellom forvaltningsoppgåver, rådgjeving, testing, dokumentasjon og opplæring. Du vert ein del av IKT og dokumentsenter og skal samarbeide med tekniske ressursar, informasjonstryggleik, personvern, dokumentforvalting og fagmiljø i kommunen. review_candidates.description: In the last year we have grown at a record pace, from expanding our insurance and lending teams to growing our mortgage teams and our recent acquisition into the real estate sector, this all means more staff, in more locations. To support our growing teams our IT department are often one of the first to interact with new colleagues, from setting up user accounts and ensuring that they have the right equipment in place, to making sure that our systems remain robust and secure. As part of this growth, we are now looking to expand our IT Team to manage the increased number of requests, by bringing in a first line support administrator. What will you be doing? Act as the first point of contact for IT support requests coming in via phone, email, in person or our IT Ticketing system. Log, track and manage support tickets in line with our service level policies Diagnose and resolve common hardware or software issues. Assist in user and device management, on/off boarding users and devices as well as managing permissions. Supporting the IT Manager with change projects including the deployment of new systems, conducting needs analysis and maintaining platform licenses. About You: You may already be working in IT support, or you may be looking to get your first role, but you are already comfortable using Windows 11 and the Microsoft 365 suite. You will have some experience dealing with customers either by phone or face to face, either in retail or hospitality, or you may be looking to return to an office role following a career break. You already have some knowledge of IT Fundamentals, either through formal study, such as A Levels or a BTEC Diploma, or self-study. You are a natural ‘people’ person with great communication and interpersonal skills and the ability to deal with enquiries at all levels. You have a great eye for detail and a proactive approach to getting things done, and an analytical approach to problem-solving. We are seeking an individual that is self-motivated, and able to provide evidence of personal development through training. If you would like to join a friendly and supportive team and are already based in Guernsey, we would love to hear from you.
